subject: postgres
title: Automate a daily database health report
prompt: How would you structure a daily PostgreSQL and MongoDB health check that processes results into a CSV, including error handling and maintainability?
answer: Treat the checks as independent adapters behind a common interface: each connects with a timeout, gathers a defined set of measurements, and returns records with a timestamp, system, check name, value and status. For PostgreSQL, a successful authenticated SELECT 1 checks more than server reachability; pg_stat_activity can also support an agreed connection-usage check. Specify which MongoDB checks and thresholds the service owners need rather than inventing them from the question. Keep connection settings outside the code, use least-privilege credentials from a secret store, and close every connection even when a check fails. Exact PostgreSQL statistics fields and access privileges depend on the deployed version and role.

Run each adapter independently so a MongoDB timeout does not suppress the PostgreSQL result, and record failures explicitly rather than writing a misleading healthy value. Normalize results in a shared processing function, then write CSV with a fixed header using a CSV library; write to a temporary file and replace the destination only after a complete report is ready. Schedule the job daily, alert when the job or a check fails, avoid logging secrets, and test success, timeout, authentication failure and CSV escaping with controlled fixtures. Statistics may be cached within a transaction and cumulative counters may lag, so use short transactions and include collection time; a daily report alone cannot detect every short outage.
pitfalls: Treating an unreachable database as a healthy zero measurement.
Allowing one failed adapter to prevent all other checks from reporting.
Exposing credentials or assuming statistics update instantaneously.
followups: How would you distinguish a failed check from a missing report?
Which checks and alert thresholds would you agree with service owners?
